I grepped Mathlib for uses of the rangeIcc and rangeSingleton lemmas. `rangeSingleton` uses `@[simps]`, and the `mem_rangeSingleton_apply_iff` and `mem_rangeIcc_apply_iff` lemmas are already covered by the generated apply lemmas plus `mem_singleton` and `mem_Icc`. I did not run Lean, so I did not check the exact form of the generated `rangeIcc_apply`. I am inferring it from how `@[simps apply]` works on a `toFun` field. That is the main uncertainty. findings.excerpt: lemma coe_rangeIcc (f g : ι →₀ α) : rangeIcc f g i = Icc (f i) (g i) := rfl
findings.problem: `rangeIcc` is declared with `@[simps apply]`. That attribute already generates a simp lemma `Finsupp.rangeIcc_apply` stating `rangeIcc f g i = Icc (f i) (g i)`, which is the same statement as `coe_rangeIcc`. The hand-written lemma is therefore a non-simp duplicate of the canonical simp lemma. It also has a misleading `coe_` name, since there is no coercion to rewrite. It is only used in `card_Icc` via `simp_rw`. The sibling DFinsupp file names its analogue `rangeIcc_apply`, so the two files are inconsistent. Two parallel rewrite rules for one normal form make it unclear which one callers should use.
findings.proposed_change: Delete `coe_rangeIcc` and use the simps-generated `rangeIcc_apply` in `card_Icc`, either in `simp_rw [Icc_eq, card_finsupp, rangeIcc_apply]` or by letting `simp` close it. If the explicit statement is wanted, drop `apply` from `@[simps apply]` and mark the explicit lemma `@[simp] theorem rangeIcc_apply`, as the DFinsupp file does. Either way there should be exactly one simp-normal rule `rangeIcc f g i = Icc (f i) (g i)`.
findings.benefit: Callers get one canonical simp lemma for evaluating `rangeIcc` at a point. The naming matches `DFinsupp.rangeIcc_apply`, and the redundant declaration goes away.

evidence.excerpt:
@[simps apply]
def rangeIcc (f g : ι →₀ α) : ι →₀ Finset α where
theorem rangeIcc_apply (f g : Π₀ i, α i) (i : ι) : f.rangeIcc g i = Icc (f i) (g i) := rfl
